title: Align active prompts and reviewer contracts with accepted audit
goal: Make the active coding, repair, reviewer and primary-orchestration instructions match the accepted repository audit before normal autonomous implementation resumes.
scope: Protected governance-only task. Do not change product/domain/compiler/generator/TIA worker behavior, workflows, provider runtime, runner configuration, secrets, vendor payloads, or IndustrialMDE.

Align agents/prompts/coder.md with bounded task authority, positive task scope, explicit blocker classes, no Git publication, no direct Windows/TIA access, and READY_FOR_REVIEW|BLOCKED finish semantics.

Align agents/prompts/repair.md with additive same-task repair, one bounded review/repair attempt, positive allowedPaths, conditional TiaV21Worker opt-in, opencode.json protection, and fail-closed blocker classification.

Retire agents/prompts/reviewer-requirements.md and agents/prompts/reviewer-tia.md as non-authoritative compatibility redirects; canonical review instructions remain reviews/templates/code-review.md and reviews/templates/plc-review.md with one shared reviews/schemas/external-review-response.schema.json contract.
Move the useful requirement-by-requirement lens into canonical CODE_REVIEW and provenance/TIA evidence rules into canonical PLC_REVIEW.
Add accepted primary-orchestrator priorities to the existing normative AGENTS.md contract rather than creating an unused orchestrator prompt.
Update docs/AGENT_AUTONOMY.md where it still describes obsolete Gemini provider and dual-review behavior.
Add deterministic prompt-alignment regressions under the existing ExternalReviewProtocol test discovery path.

requirements: agents/prompts/coder.md names the four blocker classes CANDIDATE_DEFECT, INFRASTRUCTURE_DEFECT, MISSING_EVIDENCE and EXTERNAL_TIA_BLOCKER and ends work as READY_FOR_REVIEW or BLOCKED.

agents/prompts/repair.md no longer categorically forbids src/TiaV21Worker/**; worker edits require both trusted candidatePolicy.allowTiaV21WorkerChanges=true and positive allowedPaths coverage, while opencode.json remains protected.
Legacy reviewer prompt files are explicitly RETIRED and direct readers to canonical CODE_REVIEW/PLC_REVIEW templates plus the shared response schema; no active workflow/runtime references them.
reviews/templates/code-review.md requires criterion-by-criterion acceptance evaluation and forbids treating unexecuted checks as PASS.
reviews/templates/plc-review.md is provenance-first, distinguishes qualification/reuse/reference-compile evidence, and forbids PASS for unexecuted or unbound TIA checks.

AGENTS.md contains the accepted primary orchestration priorities: time-to-first-usable-device, bounded tasks, one independent reviewer by default, merged-main TIA, product implementation delegated to coding agents by default, and no optional infrastructure/doc work ahead of the active product route without a concrete blocker.

docs/AGENT_AUTONOMY.md reflects OpenRouter-first/DeepSeek fallback, contained candidate/publisher separation, conditional worker scope and canonical reviewer templates instead of obsolete Gemini/dual-review instructions.
Deterministic Linux prompt-alignment tests are green and existing ExternalReviewProtocol/FactoryIsolation/SiemensBackend/generator regressions remain green.
tia: No Windows/TIA execution is required for this governance-only task.
